The Ensuring Lasting Smiles Act (H.R. 3277) mandates coverage for congenital anomaly treatments, including dental and reconstructive care. While the intent to help families like Kairi’s is commendable, the bill’s Section 2(a)(3)(A)(ii) expands coverage to “adjunctive dental… support” without cost controls, risking premium spikes.

Bureaucrats already weaponize coverage gaps—now they’ll exploit vague terms like “secondary conditions” (Section 2(a)(3)(A)(iii)) to inflate claims. Taxpayers deserve solutions that fix insurance denials without letting D.C. turn medical necessity into a blank check.

Audit the waste first—then fund care.

The real test is whether Congress will close loopholes or just open the floodgates—see the evidence: https://t.co/lysaylWerG

The One Big Beautiful Bill is a generational win for American families—exactly the kind of legislation that proves D.C. can prioritize real solutions over bureaucratic bloat. School choice provisions empower parents, break the zip-code lottery trap, and force failing systems to compete.

Energy dominance? Critical. Unleashing domestic production cuts reliance on foreign regimes while funding growth through strategic tariffs, not taxpayer raids. Critics whine about deficits, but static CBO models ignore dynamic gains: tax cuts driving output, deregulation fueling innovation, and energy exports offsetting debt.

This bill doesn’t just shuffle money—it rewrites the rules to favor producers over parasites. Pass it, scale it, watch America win.

Streamlining Medicare Advantage’s prior authorization process is a step toward efficiency, but H.R. 3514’s $55M electronic system rollout risks becoming another bureaucratic black hole. While reducing delays for seniors is critical, Section 3’s transparency requirements lack teeth—mandating annual reports without real penalties for insurers who game approval rates. The bill’s 75% denial reversal rate (per 2018 HHS audit data) proves insurers use prior auth as a profit tool, not care safeguard.

Real reform requires dismantling the administrative bloat that lets middlemen pocket $27B annually in MA overhead instead of funding frontline care. Modernization without Medicare Advantage plan accountability just digitizes the grift.
